page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated cloud server configured with 20 shared vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The system features 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.8 GB of RAM per core. It integrates two NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage, meaning storage resources must be attached externally.

The hardware profile presents specific architectural tradeoffs. While the system offers substantial memory capacity and dual GPU accelerators, the 20 vCPUs are allocated on a shared basis rather than dedicated cores. This shared CPU allocation can introduce performance variability under sustained, CPU-heavy non-GPU workloads. However, for workloads that offload the primary computational burden to the dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs, this configuration provides a cost-efficient alternative to instances with fully dedicated physical cores, optimizing resource density for GPU-centric tasks.

This server is designed for workloads that benefit from GPU acceleration and high system memory. Appropriate use cases include machine learning inference, medium-scale AI model training, data science pipelines, video transcoding, and 3D rendering. The inclusion of one complimentary public IPv4 address supports direct network connectivity for these distributed processing tasks.
